figures.caption_checked: The caption beneath the embed ("Adoption as a state transition. ...") states the reading the diagram is meant to carry and does not restate the figure's title, so it is not a finding.

findings.summary: The rendered image carries no backdrop: 605,504 of its 1,008,000 pixels are fully transparent (alpha 0), so the figure's contrast is decided by whatever surface it lands on. Over the white page the text reads (body #333 12.63:1, title #111 18.88:1, green annotation 4.25:1); composited over black the same two text colours measure 1.66:1 and 1.11:1 and the title and arrow annotations disappear. Every other figure reviewed from this backlog could be given a white backdrop without loss.

The adoption precondition — "compose claim: projection is the source's own DD path and no producer holds it" — is set in #2E8B57 at about 12 px, which measures 4.25:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for text at that size. It is the one sentence that separates adoption from the refused collision below it, so it should be the most legible label rather than the least.

Box body text renders as a 11-14 px glyph band on a 1400 px canvas (about 10 pt at the canvas width), below the 14 pt floor this repository sets for figure text; in a column narrower than the canvas it is scaled down with the rest of the figure and becomes the smallest thing a reader has to read.

The two lower panels place about 60 words of running prose inside the image, so that text is neither selectable nor searchable and does not reflow with the page; the caption restates the argument in one sentence but does not carry these two paragraphs.

item_verdicts.contrast: defect — the green annotation (#2E8B57) measures 4.25:1 against white, under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for small text, and the canvas is fully transparent so the #333 body text and #111 title fall to 1.66:1 and 1.11:1 when composited over a dark surface.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass — the ink is the five state boxes, four arrows and their labels; no key, grid or redundant series competes with them.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass — the only styling beyond strokes and text is a light grey box fill and a light green tint on the adopted state, which marks the transition the figure exists to show; no gradient, shadow or decorative panel.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass — no label is clipped (ink spans x 29-1210 of 1400 and y 22-650 of 720) and none overlaps another label or the arrows; "finalize" sits clear above its arrow and the green annotation sits in the open gap between the stub and drafted boxes.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass — at its native 1400x720 the state chain reads left to right in one scan (projection stub -> drafted, with a receipt -> source composed) with the two failure branches set apart beneath it; the smallest text is the green annotation at about 12 px and the box body at about 14 px, both legible at native size.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass — the content is a state transition with two branches, which a table cannot carry; the two lower prose panels are explanation rather than tabular data.

method: Read only. The attachment was opened with the Read tool; its alpha channel and pixel colours were measured, and it was composited over white and over black in $TMPDIR scratch solely to see the text the transparent canvas hides. No SVG and no other image was opened, listed for content or rendered. The figure's repository path is established from the reviewed tree: the embed reference and caption in docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-adopt-pending-projection-stubs.html, and the figure tree at the reviewed head, which carries adoption-state.svg and no drawing script for it.
notes: No rubric item blocks: nothing is clipped, no label overlaps another label or the data, and every label reads on the white page the figure is served on. The transparent canvas and the sub-threshold green are the two defects worth folding into a redraw, and both are cheap to fix (a white rect behind the content, and a darker green or #333 for the annotation).
